fullText.simplified:
妈妈的“魔法”

    相信每个人都会有这样的记忆：乱七八糟的房间总能在妈妈走过以后变得干净整洁；单调简单的食材总能在妈妈的手里变成美味；无聊的生活，死气沉沉的气氛也总能在妈妈回家后变得鲜活有趣起来。
    妈妈就像一个会魔法的仙女，她让我们的生活变得温暖和充满正能量。
    我上中学的时候，家里的条件不太好。爸爸在外地工作，不高的收入要养活家里六口人。为了照顾四个孩子，妈妈不得不辞职在家。除了负责孩子们的日常生活，做家务外，她还会打一些零工贴补家用。可想而知，我们的日子过得紧巴巴的。
    初三那年，老师建议我们人手一套四大名著，用来丰富我们的文学知识。要知道，在那个年代，四大名著可是奢侈品，很难买到而且还非常贵。因此，我并不打算告诉妈妈这件事。我既不想增加家里的负担，也不想让妈妈为难。
    隔壁王小虎是我的同班同学，他哥哥在市里工作，周末回家帮他从市里的书店带回了一套精美的四大名著。王小虎非常高兴，手里拿着四大名著见人就炫耀说：“快看，最新版的四大名著，从市里带回来的。我是我们班第一个买到的哦。”妈妈买菜回来，正好听到了王小虎的话。回家以后问我为什么不告诉她买书这件事。我笑了笑说：“不是大事儿，那书不好买，我借同学的看一下就行了。”妈妈看了看我没说话，就去厨房做饭了。
    一个星期后，我回到家，一进门就看见桌子上整整齐齐地摆着一套四大名著。妈妈笑咪咪地看着我说：“快看看，喜欢不喜欢？”我拿起来仔细地翻看。然后我问妈妈是从哪里买到的。妈妈神秘地说：“我用魔法变出来的呗。”我抬起头刚想说点什么，但看到妈妈额头上冒出了大颗的汗珠，我就把想说的话又咽了回去，心想：“就让妈妈做个无所不能的魔法师吧。”
    后来，那天被妈妈变出来的四大名著跟着我上了大学，上了博士，还见证了我结婚生子，我还把它交给了我的孩子，并且告诉他这是他奶奶给他爸爸最好的礼物。
    其实，我早就“识破”了妈妈的魔法。哪有什么魔法呀，唯一的魔法就是妈妈对我们的爱。为了这份爱，妈妈卖掉了家里的鸡鸭；为了这份爱，妈妈步行了十多公里；为了这份爱，妈妈跑遍了市里大大小小的书店……
    从小到大再到老，妈妈的“魔法”带给了我们每个人爱的力量，也让我们学会了如何爱别人，所以就让我们一直在妈妈的魔法里爱下去吧！
fullText.traditional:
媽媽的“魔法”

    相信每個人都會有這樣的記憶：亂七八糟的房間總能在媽媽走過以後變得乾淨整潔；單調簡單的食材總能在媽媽的手裡變成美味；無聊的生活，死氣沉沉的氣氛也總能在媽媽回家後變得鮮活有趣起來。
    媽媽就像一個會魔法的仙女，她讓我們的生活變得溫暖和充滿正能量。
    我上中學的時候，家裡的條件不太好。爸爸在外地工作，不高的收入要養活家裡六口人。為了照顧四個孩子，媽媽不得不辭職在家。除了負責孩子們的日常生活，做家務外，她還會打一些零工貼補家用。可想而知，我們的日子過得緊巴巴的。
    初三那年，老師建議我們人手一套四大名著，用來豐富我們的文學知識。要知道，在那個年代，四大名著可是奢侈品，很難買到而且還非常貴。因此，我並不打算告訴媽媽這件事。我既不想增加家裡的負擔，也不想讓媽媽為難。
    隔壁王小虎是我的同班同學，他哥哥在市裡工作，週末回家幫他從市裡的書店帶回了一套精美的四大名著。王小虎非常高興，手裡拿著四大名著見人就炫耀說：“快看，最新版的四大名著，從市裡帶回來的。我是我們班第一個買到的哦。”媽媽買菜回來，正好聽到了王小虎的話。回家以後問我為什麼不告訴她買書這件事。我笑了笑說：“不是大事兒，那書不好買，我借同學的看一下就行了。”媽媽看了看我沒說話，就去廚房做飯了。
    一個星期後，我回到家，一進門就看見桌子上整整齊齊地擺著一套四大名著。媽媽笑眯眯地看著我說：“快看看，喜歡不喜歡？”我拿起來仔細地翻看。然後我問媽媽是從哪裡買到的。媽媽神秘地說：“我用魔法變出來的唄。”我抬起頭剛想說點什麼，但看到媽媽額頭上冒出了大顆的汗珠，我就把想說的話又嚥了回去，心想：“就讓媽媽做個無所不能的魔法師吧。”
    後來，那天被媽媽變出來的四大名著跟著我上了大學，上了博士，還見證了我結婚生子，我還把它交給了我的孩子，並且告訴他這是他奶奶給他爸爸最好的禮物。
    其實，我早就“識破”了媽媽的魔法。哪有什麼魔法呀，唯一的魔法就是媽媽對我們的愛。為了這份愛，媽媽賣掉了家裡的雞鴨；為了這份愛，媽媽步行了十多公里；為了這份愛，媽媽跑遍了市裡大大小小的書店……
    從小到大再到老，媽媽的“魔法”帶給了我們每個人愛的力量，也讓我們學會了如何愛別人，所以就讓我們一直在媽媽的魔法裡愛下去吧！

sentences.traditional: 我還把它交給了我的孩子，並且告訴他這是他奶奶給他爸爸最好的禮物。
sentences.pinyin: wǒ hái bǎ tā jiāo gěi le wǒ de hái zi bìng qiě gào su tā zhè shì tā nǎi nai gěi tā bà ba zuì hǎo de lǐ wù
sentences.english: .. and they also witnessed me get married and have a child.
Then I gave the set to my child and told him it was the best gift his grandmother had ever given me, his father.

sentences.simplified: 其实，我早就“识破”了妈妈的魔法。哪有什么魔法呀，唯一的魔法就是妈妈对我们的爱。
sentences.traditional: 其實，我早就“識破”了媽媽的魔法。哪有什麼魔法呀，唯一的魔法就是媽媽對我們的愛。
sentences.pinyin: qí shí wǒ zǎo jiù shí pò le mā ma de mó fǎ nǎ yǒu shén me mó fǎ ya wéi yī de mó fǎ jiù shì mā ma duì wǒ men de ài

sentences.simplified: 为了这份爱，妈妈卖掉了家里的鸡鸭；为了这份爱，妈妈步行了十多公里；
sentences.traditional: 為了這份愛，媽媽賣掉了家裡的雞鴨；為了這份愛，媽媽步行了十多公里；
sentences.pinyin: wèi le zhè fèn ài mā ma mài diào le jiā lǐ de jī yā wèi le zhè fèn ài mā ma bù xíng le shí duō gōng lǐ
sentences.english: In fact, I had “seen through” Mom’s magic long ago. There was no magic. The only magic was Mom’s love for us.

sentences.simplified: 为了这份爱，妈妈跑遍了市里大大小小的书店……
sentences.traditional: 為了這份愛，媽媽跑遍了市裡大大小小的書店……
sentences.pinyin: wèi le zhè fèn ài mā ma pǎo biàn le shì lǐ dà dà xiǎo xiǎo de shū diàn
sentences.english: For this love, Mom sold our family’s chickens and ducks; for this love, Mom walked over 10 kilometers;
for this love, Mom scoured bookstores of all sizes in the city.

sentences.simplified: 从小到大再到老，妈妈的“魔法”带给了我们每个人爱的力量，
sentences.traditional: 從小到大再到老，媽媽的“魔法”帶給了我們每個人愛的力量，
sentences.pinyin: cóng xiǎo dào dà zài dào lǎo mā ma de mó fǎ dài gěi le wǒ men měi ge rén ài de lì liang

sentences.simplified: 也让我们学会了如何爱别人，所以就让我们一直在妈妈的魔法里爱下去吧！
sentences.traditional: 也讓我們學會了如何愛別人，所以就讓我們一直在媽媽的魔法裡愛下去吧！
sentences.pinyin: yě ràng wǒ men xué huì le rú hé ài bié ren suǒ yǐ jiù ràng wǒ men yì zhí zài mā ma de mó fǎ lǐ ài xià qù ba
sentences.english: From childhood to adulthood and then to our later years, our moms’ “magic” has brought us the power of love.

sentence_translations: Mom’s “Magic”
I believe everyone has such memories: Messy rooms always became clean and tidy after Mom walked past them;
monotonous and simple ingredients always turned into delicious dishes in Mom’s hands;
boring days and a lifeless atmosphere always became lively and interesting when Mom came home.
Mom was like a magic fairy who made our lives warm and full of positive energy.
When I was in high school, my family’s circumstances were not good.
Dad worked in another city, and he had to support our family of six with a low income.
In order to take care of the four children, Mom had to leave her job and stay at home.
In addition to taking care of the children’s daily life and doing housework,  ..
.. she also took some odd jobs to make additional money to support the family.
As you can imagine, we were hard up.
In the third year of junior high school, ..
.. our teacher suggested that we all should get a set of the Four Classic Novels to enrich our knowledge of literature.
You know, in those days, the Four Classic Novels were luxury items. They were very hard to get and very expensive.
Therefore, I didn’t plan to tell Mom about this.
I didn’t want to bring any extra burden to the family, and I didn’t want to put Mom in a difficult situation.
Wang Xiaohu lived next door and was my classmate.
His older brother worked in the city, ..
.. and brought him a beautiful set of the Four Classic Novels from a bookstore in the city when he came home at the weekend.
Wang Xiaohu was very happy and showed off his Four Classic Novels:
“Look, this is the latest edition of the Four Classic Novels brought back from the city.
I’m the first one in our class to get it.”
Mom came back from grocery shopping and happened to hear what Wang Xiaohu said.
When we got home, she asked me why I didn’t tell her about buying these books.
I smiled and said, “It’s no big deal. It’s hard to get those books. I’ll just borrow them from my classmates to read them.”
Mom looked at me without saying anything, and then she went to the kitchen to make dinner.
A week later, I came home, and as soon as I came in through the door, I saw a set of the Four Classic Novels neatly laid out on the table.
Mom looked at me with a smile and said, “Take a look. Do you like it?”
I picked up the books and carefully looked them over. Then I asked Mom where she bought them.
Mom said mysteriously, “I made them with magic.”
I looked up to say something, but when I saw large beads of sweat appearing on Mom’s forehead, ..
..  I swallowed what I wanted to say and thought, “Let Mom be an omnipotent magician.”
Later, the Four Great Books that were conjured up by my mother that day followed me through college, and when I did my Ph.D., ..
.. and they also witnessed me get married and have a child.
Then I gave the set to my child and told him it was the best gift his grandmother had ever given me, his father.
In fact, I had “seen through” Mom’s magic long ago. There was no magic. The only magic was Mom’s love for us.
For this love, Mom sold our family’s chickens and ducks; for this love, Mom walked over 10 kilometers;
for this love, Mom scoured bookstores of all sizes in the city.
From childhood to adulthood and then to our later years, our moms’ “magic” has brought us the power of love.
It also taught us how to love other people. So let’s keep on loving with our moms’ magic!
